nonvacuity: Compiled in scratch/Check.lean: E=Unit, t=c=1/2, finite positive support, equal arm supports, and epsilon=1/4. The sole denominator is one; these masses realize a binary-treatment probability law with both arms positive.

A closed statement with four actual atoms of masses (3/8,1/8,1/8,3/8). Independent Lean checks from Defs establish nonnegative normalized weights, both gender probabilities 1/2, conditional means 55 and 30, ATE 5, and failure of conditional independence. The voter thresholds give exactly 20,25,60,65 no-voters out of 100 in the four relevant potential-outcome cases.

Definitionally the same nonempty four-atom model as T21, with no external premises. Its normalization, positive conditioning masses, conditional means, ATE, and conditional-independence failure are independently compiled in scratch/Check.lean.

Take Omega=Unit, its usual measurable space, mu=Dirac(()), A=empty and B=univ. Both events are measurable and A is a proper subset of B, so the reversed-gloss failure has a genuine instance. The probability-space instance is compiled in scratch/Check.lean.

Compiled: Omega=Unit with its Dirac probability and the Unit-indexed family whose sole member is univ. It is a nonempty measurable disjoint covering partition with probability-one cell. Zero-mass nonempty cells are also possible: on R with Dirac(0), the partition {0}, R minus {0} has one such cell, so the first formula is not restricted to positive cells.

The definition zeroMass gives the unique member of Fin 1 weight one; the random variable is identically zero. Its lower-tail probability is one and every point mass at 1,2,3 is zero. There are no antecedents or empty index types.
Compiled: q(k)=1 if k=0 and zero otherwise is everywhere nonnegative, summable, and has sum one. This instance has missing nonpositive mass one, so the missing-mass identity is substantive.

The concrete index set contains (0,0). At level m there are 2^m positive weights 2^(-2m-1), totaling 2^(-m-1); their geometric sum is one. The locations lie densely in (0,1), and none equals 1/3. These give a genuine countable atomic probability law and its stated CDF; no divergent-sum default is used.

The supplied six-point fair die is a nonempty instance with values 1 through 6. Nonnegative weights, total mass one, and StrictMono dieValue are compiled in scratch/Check.lean. The countable-range part also has the one-point Dirac example; the ordered finite part uses m=5 for the die.

Use normalized Lebesgue measure restricted to [0,1]. Its CDF is max(0,min(1,x)); the three explicit functions are bounded measurable functions supported in [0,1] and differ only on finite null sets. They are genuinely integrable and normalized, so their integral equalities do not use the zero value of nonintegrable Bochner integrals.

Compiled: normalLaw=gaussianReal 0 1 and normalPDF=gaussianPDFReal 0 1 satisfy Density, including the identity-map version. Their product law has productPDF as a JointDensity and both marginal densities equal normalPDF. For the separate boundary example take y=1/2; the inner derivative is the uniform CDF and fails to be differentiable at zero.

This is a closed explicit construction. Every stage retains 0 and 1. Component lengths are L_n=2^(-n-1)+2^(-2n-1), so stage measures are 1/2+2^(-n-1) and the nested closed intersection has measure 1/2. Thus the subtype is nonempty and its doubled pullback measure has total mass one. Closedness makes the inclusion a measurable embedding, excluding the zero fallback of comap.

The universal premises are realized by the compiled standard Gaussian law with X=id and its density. For the existential part, C=[0,1/2] minus Q is Borel with Lebesgue measure 1/2; put twice restricted Lebesgue measure on its subtype and take the inclusion. Its literal range is C, density is 2*indicator_C, and rational density prevents every nondegenerate interval from lying in C.

Compiled: Omega=R, X=id, g=h=id; X is surjective and takes different values at 0 and 1. Equipping R with the standard Gaussian probability gives a canonical random-variable instance as well. Arbitrary domains containing the range can be extended off their domains without affecting the equivalence.

A closed example: the open rectangle (0,1) times (-1,0) has area one. Its indicator is a normalized integrable density, its support lies inside the printed event, and it vanishes on every triangular integration section with y>=0. Thus an actual jointly continuous law gives event probability one and printed integral zero.

Compiled productLaw=standard Gaussian product and productPDF satisfy the probability and JointDensity premises. This law assigns positive mass both to the triangle and to the omitted negative-y region, so the correction and its equality criterion have nontrivial instances. Global joint integrability supplies the Fubini hypotheses almost everywhere.

There are no external premises. Real analyticity of the exact infiniteSliceDensity is independently compiled in scratch/Check.lean. Both defining denominators are strictly positive. Its y-integral is exp(x)/(1+exp(x))^2, whose x-integral is one. At y=0 the integrand tends to 1/pi, forcing the extended nonnegative integral to infinity. For y!=0 and t=exp(x), the slice integral has integrand t/[pi*(1+t)^2*(1+y^2*t^2)], bounded near zero by t/pi and for t>=1 by 1/(pi*y^2*t^3).

Compiled product Gaussian density and its marginal densities satisfy the first branch. The same Borel productPDF at x=0 has an integrable section with strictly positive integral, also compiled, so the conditional normalization branch has a genuine finite positive denominator. Finite marginal versions may additionally be changed on null sets; no extra Borel hypothesis is imposed on these versions.

The standard Gaussian input is a probability measure (compiled), and its zero multiple has law Dirac(0) with unit atom. Unit scales are strictly positive and rho=1 and rho=-1 are permitted by the printed closed parameter range; both actual normalization denominators vanish (compiled). The endpoint refutation uses these vanishing denominators, not the zero assigned to undefined ordinary quotients by Lean total division.
